what: LOSS-ONCE (2026-10-24): the trainer's loss evaluates each logit's exponential once -- a row's first 1,024 kept in double on its task's stack, its adjoints dividing the kept values, a wider row's tail evaluated again -- every adjoint, term and loss as it was. The records time the committed loss against the tree before it, and the PR818 study's models with once_level3.py: the same edit to each of the study's three trainer forks, and in the geometric heads (global, query_full) the gate's exponential a task's 512 elements at a time through the tensor unit's span entry (bcir_tensor_exp), where the fork calls bcir_tensor_expf an element; every trained state and logit as it was
host: Intel(R) Xeon(R) Processor @ 2.30GHz, 4 vCPU (4 cores, one thread each; AVX-512F, AMX), 2 MiB of L2 a core, 260 MiB of L3; Linux 6.18; clang 18.1.3 and GCC 13.3 (-std=c11 -O3 -ffp-contract=off -fno-math-errno -pthread; the study's builds with GCC, as the study builds them); Python 3.11.15, NumPy 2.2.6, torch 2.13.0+cu130 (CPU); OMP_WAIT_POLICY=PASSIVE, OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1
